_about.purpose: Single source of truth for every quantitative claim in this project. results/README.md is GENERATED from this file by scripts/render_results.py, so numbers cannot drift between the two.

provenance_status.transcribed: Number is recorded here from the run's stdout, which was captured in the git commit message at the listed SHA. The raw artifact (JSON/log/NEFF) is NOT in the repo — see _artifact_loss.
provenance_status.reproduced: Original number is transcribed AND an independent re-run on the replacement instance is committed under results/raw/. The committed artifact carries the re-run's value, which is recorded alongside. See _reproduction for the agreement.
provenance_status.in_repo: Raw artifact is committed under results/raw/ and is the source of the number quoted here.

_about._artifact_loss: The trn2 instance used for the ORIGINAL measurements expired on 2026-08-02. Every raw artifact lived in /tmp on that host: measure_mfu --json-out files, neuron-explorer summary-json output, NEFF/NTFF profile pairs, and detached run logs. All are gone, permanently — a re-run produces new artifacts, not the lost ones. The original numbers survive because each run's stdout was pasted into the commit message at the time, and every producing script is committed. Every measurement has since been re-run on a replacement instance and those artifacts ARE committed (see _reproduction), so each number is now backed by a raw file plus an independent confirmation. Logged as sticking point #17: results should never have lived only on an ephemeral host, and the fix was one default path per script, not new code.

_reproduction.why: The original host expired before any raw artifact was committed. Re-running everything on a replacement is the only way to turn transcribed numbers back into evidence, and it doubles as an independent check: a number that reproduces on different physical hardware is not a fluke of one instance.

_about.hardware: trn2.3xlarge, 1 Neuron device, 4 NeuronCores, LNC2 (2 logical cores), single logical core used unless stated
_about.compiler_flags: NEURON_CC_FLAGS unset for every measurement — compiler defaults throughout. This was the top open item, on the theory that a bad default could be the whole slowdown. Now CLOSED in both halves by two controls that sweep {unset, --target trn2, +--lnc 1, +--lnc 2, +-O2}. Wall clock: NKI is invariant at 1.02x spread (13.82-14.15 ms). Device: NKI is invariant at 1.05x spread (0.580-0.608 ms) and its marginal HBM traffic is 6.29 MB/call under every setting, which is exactly the unfused floor — one tile in, one tile out — so no flag has anywhere to go. See the compiler-flag-control and device-time-under-flags measurements.

denominator.note: MFU denominator, stated explicitly because Trn2 has two conventions plus an LNC subtlety.
denominator.source: Cayman architecture doc; 632 is TensorEngine-only, 667 published includes VectorE + ScalarE

measurements.what: CONTROL: does the NKI/torch gap depend on NEURON_CC_FLAGS? Runs first, because a bad compiler default would invalidate every measurement below it.
measurements.method: 28 chained SiLU applications, tile [512,3072] bf16, wall clock. One subprocess and one isolated compile cache per setting, so no setting inherits another's cache. Absolute times are not comparable across settings; the ratio is the measurement.
measurements.verdict: NKI is INVARIANT across compiler settings — 13.82 to 14.15 ms, 1.02x spread. No setting rescues the NKI path, so the gap is not a compiler-flag artifact.
measurements.scope_limit: Measures WALL time. 13.82 ms / 28 calls = 0.494 ms/call, which is the post-fix dispatch floor, so this run is ~97% dispatch. It establishes that the DISPATCH cost is flag-invariant and does NOT by itself settle whether the DEVICE-time gap in Findings #25/#26 depends on flags.
measurements.notes: The first version of this probe thresholded on whether the RATIO moved, saw 1.53x spread, and read that as 'flags matter'. Reading the columns separately reverses it: the spread is one setting (--lnc 1) making TORCH 2.3x slower, which flatters the ratio without helping NKI at all. A ratio can move because its denominator moved. The verdict logic now reports the NKI and torch spreads separately and concludes on whether NKI itself responds.

measurements.what: CONTROL, part 2: does the DEVICE-time gap depend on NEURON_CC_FLAGS? The wall-clock control above is ~97% dispatch by construction, so it could not answer this.
measurements.method: SiLU profiled at N=1 and N=28 under each of the five flag settings, one isolated compile cache per setting so no setting can serve another's NEFF. Reports device time at N=28 and, more diagnostically, marginal HBM traffic per call solved from the two call counts.
measurements.verdict: No setting makes NKI faster than torch on device, and NKI's marginal traffic stays pinned at exactly 6.29 MB/call — the unfused floor — under every setting. The device gap is STRUCTURAL: an opaque custom call cannot be fused into its neighbours and no compiler flag reaches that.
measurements.why_this_is_the_strong_form: The result is not 'we tried five settings and none was better', which would leave a sixth setting open. It is that the quantity a better setting would have to move is already at its theoretical minimum. NKI moves one tile in and one tile out per call, which is the least an unfusable op can move. There is no headroom for a flag to find.
measurements.lnc1_caveat: The 1.35x at --lnc 1 is the best ratio in the table and is NOT an improvement: NKI barely moves (0.608 -> 0.580) while torch gets 91% slower (0.224 -> 0.429). Reading it as progress is the same mistake the first version of the wall-clock control made.
measurements.notes: Together with compiler-flag-control this closes the project's top open item in both halves: dispatch cost is flag-invariant (1.02x NKI spread on wall clock) and device cost is flag-invariant (1.05x NKI spread, 1.00x marginal-traffic spread). Findings #25 and #26 stand as measured.

measurements.what: Qwen3-0.6B forward, all 3 NKI kernels, seq 512, WITH the Finding #24 fix
measurements.notes: IQRs non-overlapping vs baseline. Residual added cost = 141.43 - 42.04 = 99.39 ms over 169 calls = 0.588 ms/call. The reproduction gives 146.67 - 44.36 = 102.31 ms over 169 = 0.605 ms/call, so the per-call residual reproduces to within 3%.

measurements.what: Qwen3-0.6B forward, no kernels, seq 2048
Qwen3-0.6B forward, all 3 NKI kernels, seq 2048, WITH the fix
measurements.notes: Amortisation test: call count is fixed by model depth, so more sequence = more work per call. 2.59x more baseline work costs only 1.16x more per call, so the residual is near-fixed and the penalty nearly halves. This is the most encouraging measurement in the project for the approach's viability: the per-call overhead does not scale with the work, so at production sequence lengths it matters proportionally less.

measurements.what: Qwen3-0.6B forward, NKI SiLU only, seq 512, WITHOUT the fix
measurements.notes: Per-call attribution: 51.9 ms/call, matching the all-three figure of 51.6 ms/call. Uniformity across kernels is what pointed at a fixed per-invocation cost.

measurements.what: Finding #24 fix, two independent methods, one process, baseline re-run last as control
measurements.notes: The override is set to whatever _detect_target() returns on the host, never hardcoded, because a wrong target would compile for the wrong hardware and could be silently wrong. cos_sim identical to 6 dp across all four, so neither fix changes what gets compiled. Baseline is re-run LAST as a control: 52.11 then 52.07 ms/call, within 0.1%, which rules out ordering or warm-up as the cause of the speedup.

measurements.what: Do N NKI calls share one XLA graph and one device execution? Counted via torch-xla ExecuteTime metric.
measurements.notes: compiles=0 on every variant, 3 samples each within 0.1%. The 28 calls DID share one graph (196 nodes = 28x7) and still cost 28x, so graph batching was never the lever. execs-before-mark_step = 0 rules out nki.jit self-synchronising. The torch control (C, D) is what makes the negative result trustworthy: 28 torch ops also collapse to 1 execution, so the counter demonstrably detects batching.

measurements.what: Where the wall time goes for a 28-NKI-call graph
measurements.notes: torch-xla metric accumulators are NANOSECONDS; an earlier read of them as seconds produced a nine-digit millisecond figure. Cross-check against metrics_report(), which prints explicit units. CompileTime must be 0 or the run is measuring compilation rather than dispatch; it is asserted, not assumed.

before_fix.attribution: 51 of 52 ms in select.poll <- subprocess.check_output <- _detect_target <- resolve_target <- _compile_opts

after_fix.attribution: create_computation <- xla_op_registry <- nki/framework/_torch_xla.py, plus pyhlo scribe x56 and protobuf enum lookups x168

measurements.notes: Calls timed with NO mark_step and NO sync, so the cost is proven synchronous inside the call rather than deferred.

measurements.what: neuron-explorer profile of the NEFF containing 28 NKI SiLU calls
measurements.notes: activate_instruction_count 112 = 28 x 4 confirms all 28 calls are in this one NEFF. 0.609 ms device against 1459 ms wall is the 2400x ratio that ruled out every device-side explanation at once. This single comparison did more work than any other measurement in the project: it eliminated real compute, per-custom-call launch cost and an emitted barrier simultaneously, because none of them can hide in 0.6 ms.

measurements.what: Device time, NKI kernel vs the torch op it replaces, identical work both ways

marginal_traffic_regression.note: traffic(N) = FIXED + N x MARGINAL, solved from the N=1 and N=28 points. Unfused floor for a [512,3072] bf16 tile is 2 tiles = 6.29 MB.

reproduced.note: Every one of the eight rows above landed within 0.5% on the replacement instance, and both structural conclusions are exact.
reproduced.interpretation: torch's marginal traffic being ~0 while its fixed traffic is exactly 2 tiles is the direct evidence for fusion: 28 chained torch ops move no more HBM than one, which is only possible if the chain collapsed into a single pass. NKI's 6.29 MB/call is precisely one read in and one write out.

measurements.notes: CHAINED microbenchmark: 28 identical ops back to back. This maximises the compiler's fusion opportunity and is therefore NKI's worst case. Do not quote the 2.5-2.7x ratio without the in-situ figure below. NKI marginal traffic is exactly the unfused floor, so the kernels spill nothing and the gap is the forfeited fusion, not kernel quality. Do NOT divide total traffic by N: the fixed 12.58 MB of NEFF setup traffic dominates at N=1 and produced a false '3.00x the floor, the kernels spill an fp32 intermediate' reading before the two-point regression separated fixed from marginal.

measurements.what: Real Qwen3-0.6B forward: how much of the regression is device vs dispatch
measurements.robustness: The split has now been computed from FOUR independent wall-time pairs across two physical instances: 46.65/146.65, 47.52/144.19, 50.138/144.65 and 54.783/153.43. Device share lands at 8.4%, 8.6%, 8.9% and 8.5%; the projection at 1.18x, 1.18x, 1.17x and 1.15x. The conclusion does not depend on which pair is used.
measurements.precision_note: The two inputs have very different precision, and it is the imprecise one the projection leans on. Device time is highly repeatable — baseline 14.318 / 14.329 / 14.330 ms and kernelized 22.676 / 22.696 / 22.722 / 22.740 ms, a spread of ~0.3% — because neuron-explorer reads a hardware trace of a fixed NEFF. Wall time swings 17% across the same runs (46.65 to 54.78 ms baseline) because it includes host scheduling. So the DEVICE GAP of ~8.4 ms is the solid quantity and should be quoted as such; the percentage and the projection inherit the wall time's noise and are worth quoting as ranges (8.4-8.9% device, 1.15-1.18x projected) rather than as point estimates.
measurements.notes: THIS IS THE NUMBER TO LEAD WITH. Wall times here come from the profiled run rather than from measure_mfu, because NEURON_RT_INSPECT adds a few ms; the decomposition must use one consistent pair, and an earlier version mixed walls from an expired host with device times from a fresh one. profile_model_device_time.py now writes wall_times.json and the summary reads it, so a run cannot mix eras. HBM traffic includes weights, so the 1.42x ratio dilutes the activation-only effect and is not the fusion penalty directly. The projection was hand-computed in the original run; sum_model_device_time.py now emits it, so it cannot drift from the walls it is derived from.

measurements.what: nkilib fused MLP vs torch (3 matmuls + silu), device time, distinct weights per block
measurements.status_note: The H=1024/I=3072 pair is reproduced; the H=4096/I=4096 pair is transcribed only, because the harness profiles the Qwen3-0.6B shape and the larger shape was a separate manual invocation.

reproduced.note: Each profile directory legitimately contains TWO NEFFs: the correctness check executes a 1-block graph, the timed loop executes a 28-block graph. They are told apart by instruction count (24 vs 672 for NKI). For the NKI path the 1-block graph also carries the on-device weight transpose, which is why it costs 3.534 ms and 1172 MB against torch's 0.122 ms and 24 MB — that difference IS the weight-layout cost, isolated by accident and then kept.

weight_transpose_cost.note: Finding #17 (weight layout) quantified. Separate NEFF, one-time at load rather than per step.

measurements.notes: H=1024/I=3072 is Qwen3-0.6B's MLP shape and is INSIDE Finding #18's compile limit, so this kernel works for the benchmarked model. A first version of this measurement shared one weight set across all 28 blocks, letting the compiler amortise one weight load; torch showed 12.1 MB/block against an 18.9 MB weight set, which exposed it. Fixed to per-block weights (528 MB total).

measurements.what: Fused MLP single-core compile boundary vs intermediate_size
measurements.conclusion: passes iff intermediate_size <= 4096; boundary is between 4096 and 4224; not a ratio effect
measurements.error: 'floordiv' does not allow division by zero, in nkilib/core/utils/kernel_helpers.py:104 via mlp_cte_tile_info.py:236
measurements.notes: REFRAMED by Finding #26: this is a design boundary, not a bug. A floordiv by zero on a shard-count calculation is what happens with no SPMD shard grid. Originally filed as an nki-library bug to fix. The reframe matters for the recommendation: 'the library has a bug at I>4096' invites a bug report, whereas 'the library assumes a multi-core shard grid we are not giving it' invites the correct question, which is whether per-layer swapping is the right integration model for these kernels at all.

measurements.what: Is torch.compile broken on this stack? (Finding #23)
measurements.root_cause: torch_neuronx replaces certain ATen ops with XLA user computations. The dispatch predicate is `if any(is_xla_tensor(it) or is_xla_device(it) ...)`, which a FakeTensor on xla:0 satisfies, so Dynamo's fake-tensor pass is routed into _xla_user_computation and rejected. No abstract impls.
measurements.workaround: torch_xla.compile() works; verified same value as eager (sum = 902.0360)

reproduced.delta: same pass/fail pattern. The absolute sum differs from the original run's 902.0360 because the input is randomly generated; what the check asserts is that the two paths agree WITH EACH OTHER, which they do to 4 dp.

measurements.notes: Affected list includes Embedding, Softmax and CrossEntropyLoss, so this hits essentially any transformer. Unrelated to the Kernel Hub; filed because we found it.

open_items.item: CLOSED — is any of this a compiler-flag artifact?
open_items.detail: Was the top open item, on the theory that a bad compiler default could be the entire slowdown. Closed in both halves. Dispatch: NKI wall time is invariant across {unset, --target trn2, +--lnc 1, +--lnc 2, +-O2} at 1.02x spread. Device: NKI device time is invariant at 1.05x spread and NKI marginal HBM traffic is 6.29 MB/call — exactly the unfused floor — under every setting, so there is no headroom for a flag to find. Both probes run as harness stages, so a future stack change re-tests it automatically rather than requiring someone to remember.
open_items.status: closed 2026-07-29, see the compiler-flag-control and device-time-under-flags measurements

open_items.item: Is the per-call create_computation rebuild cacheable?
open_items.detail: 91.6% of the remaining regression. Not attempted: inside torch_xla's op-registry path, and a wrong guess could be silently incorrect rather than error.

open_items.item: Can a NKI custom call participate in compiler fusion?
open_items.detail: Decides whether the last ~18% after the dispatch fix is recoverable.

open_items.item: Does a kernel spanning a fused region beat the compiler on that region?
open_items.detail: The fused MLP answers this for single-core (no, by ~3x). Unmeasured multi-core with an SPMD grid, which is the configuration the kernel was built for.
